title: SGD, momentum, RMSProp, Adam
summary: What each optimizer accumulates, and what the normal equations cost instead.

choices.text: Adam reaches a better minimum than SGD on every problem, so it should replace SGD wherever a gradient is available.
Stochastic gradient descent estimates the gradient on a minibatch. On a linear model, one step with batch size B costs O(Bd); that step does not have to read all n rows.
RMSProp keeps a moving average of squared gradients and multiplies the step by its square root, so a coordinate with a consistently huge gradient takes a larger step.
For dense linear regression, forming and solving the normal equations costs O(nd² + d³). One full pass of gradient descent on the same squared loss costs O(nd).
Momentum keeps an exponentially decayed sum of past gradients (a velocity) and steps along that velocity, which damps zig-zags when curvature differs by direction.
Adam keeps a momentum-like first moment and an RMSProp-like second moment, and it bias-corrects both because they start at zero and would otherwise stay shrunk.
